answer: Hardware TPM attestation ties one identity to one physical chip. A node asks its TPM 2.0 for a signed quote and sends it with the endorsement certificate. The registry checks the vendor chain and binds one identity per chip serial. Every 24 hours the node must re-attest or it drops out. A ripple of fake agents needs real silicon, so 1,000 fakes means 1,000 TPM boards at about $15 each plus $400 a month hosting, and an onyx-black market cert fails the vendor check. A raven can't wear ten bodies. Think of a concert wristband: one body, one band, no exceptions.
